changes.evidence: Between the accented à and the tall l of localiser there is a separate low two-part connected group: an initial short s-like hook and a returning e stroke. It is live text, not part of the preceding accent.

The exponent is one short unfooted upright stroke of the same height and form as the adjacent prime of T'. In the following line the explicitly written 1 has both an upper entry and a foot. Prime is transcribed as drawn here, without changing it to the affine-dimension reading the context would suggest.
The separator between E and T' is a distinct oblique stroke sloping down to the right. The letter baselines slope the other way, so this is not a horizontal minus merely tilted with the row.

After the final S' on the line containing i.e. there is one descending comma stroke. The upper detached stroke is S's prime; there is no additional point at the punctuation position to make a semicolon.

A dark tall digit-like stem after the live 2 has diagonal cancellation strokes through it, before the following comma. Its presence is certain; the underlying 1 is not fully separable from the cancellation and remains doubtful.

Above the doubled-stem E there is a short, unfooted, slightly slanting stroke. It matches the prime-form of the first equation and is unlike the footed 1 in the intervening E^1_S. The printed notation therefore keeps the prime-shaped written mark.

The word after Et on has a low initial a/c group, a tall h, a detached accent and a short ve ending. It has neither the long l nor the final crossed t that conclut would require. Et on is also visible and uncancelled.
The line ends with the large OK; the blank after its K contains no separate point.

The initial long mark is a bracket, with an upper horizontal arm and a long upright at the left of one Considérons. That word is not struck. There is no second written Considérons in this opening. The curved line after the word belongs to the insertion leader for donc.
The word donc is written above the baseline. Its curved leader descends into the gap after Considérons and before les; it is an insertion at that position, not part of the line above.

Blind and cross-leaf review: the sign has an upper horizontal bar and a lower bar with a hooked entry; there is no distinct sequence of m humps. It matches the small two-stroke shorthand on 086/091 and differs from the clearly barred capital M on 097. Transcribe the written equals sign, retaining its expansion only in the abbreviation list.

The first line ends with the full live word anneau and a hyphen. The next line begins with jauge, including its dotted j and long g descender, immediately followed by an opening parenthesis before the second anneau. None of this text is cancelled.

The strike crosses the entire phrase but stops before the live point. The q descender and i mark of qui survive. The initial small curved/tall group is compatible with ce or et; the last word has an ascender and obscured low turns, admitting donne/devra and the blind reader’s leur. Keep those limits explicit instead of resolving covered letters.

The small text reads au dessus de x without a hyphen. Its enclosing/leading line bends down into the gap after the lower-row barred K and before the closing parenthesis. It is attached there; placing it immediately after correspondent detaches it from the actual leader endpoint.

The compact retraced group after dans has a looped rising entry and low return compatible with le, but its merged strokes also admit a cursive E. No independent cancellation stroke can be isolated from those strokes. Keep le first with E as an alternative, live, rather than claiming certain letters or a certain deletion.
The second donc is above the running line. Its curved insertion stroke reaches the space between opère and dans; the word therefore attaches before dans. The stroke does not cancel dans.
The final Galois-group parenthesis is close to the right edge. No independent punctuation point follows it on the visible paper; no terminal stop is supplied.
A narrow 8 with two loops followed by a curved 2 and long lower stroke is written separately at the extreme lower-left edge.

The entire final mathematical term has a short unfooted exponent stroke. The page supplies a visibly footed 1 in its middle E occurrence; the final mark is instead the prime-form.
Two principal strokes: an upper bar and a hooked lower bar, without independent m humps. Cross-leaf comparison confirms the same equals shorthand on 086/091, distinct from barred capital M on 097.

notes:
Upright manuscript subject notes, with author page number 41 at the top and separate narrow folio 82 at lower left. Line count 23 means 20 principal running-text baselines plus three inserted-word/phrase baselines, excluding the two page numerals. There are two prose paragraphs and no standalone display, diagram or drawing. The second paragraph begins with a large bracket and remains open at the end of this page; no matching closing bracket is supplied. The first paragraph treats the genus-zero case by a section at infinity, identifies f with a section, invokes the written normality/codimension condition, and ends Et on achève ... OK. The second paragraph introduces irreducible divisors, local valuation rings, their normalization and a stabilizer acting on a residue-field closure. X in les pts x_i de X is plainly written and has not been changed to S. The varying indices x_i and x elsewhere are likewise preserved. The doubled-stem E of the affine-space terms differs visibly from the cursive group E_K; the source-shaped prime exponents at the first and last affine E are preserved, while the middle E has a fully formed 1. This is a visual distinction, not a mathematical correction: the section argument would ordinarily suggest affine dimension 1 throughout. The lower trace of the g in prolonge is its descender/return, not a separate underline. In contrast sur on the final line has its own straight underline. The three insertions were traced individually: donc after Considérons, au dessus de x after barred K inside the parenthesis, and donc after opère. The two deletions are the digit after live 2 and the phrase ce qui donne/devra; both retain doubts where the underlying strokes are obscured. The point after the latter deletion survives outside the cancellation. All three supplied C marks were cropped, and both nested deletion doubts, absent from that supplied mark list, were also cropped and retained. No mathematical theorem, extension assertion, or surjectivity claim was independently proved or used in this reading; all consistency remarks here concern local notation and attachment only. A root-flagged open place was additionally cropped once as crops/149_scan083_prolonge.png, box [415,690,1030,825]; its stroke continuity confirms that the apparent underline is the returning g descender. This adds no reading change.

Blind adjudication changes the small barred-m reading to the written equals shorthand after comparison with the same hooked lower bar on 086/091; this does not expand the abbreviation in the text. The cancelled phrase now also marks ce/et and admits leur beside donne/devra. The retraced group after N_x dans retains le/E doubt, with no securely independent strike. The first and final affine E exponents remain the short prime forms, visibly unlike the footed 1 in the middle occurrence. All 14 token-different boxes were inspected.
